paragraphs.title: Building the Burnt Offering Altar and Its Utensils

easy.question: What kind of wood was used to make the burnt offering altar?
easy.explanation: The passage says that the altar was made of shittim wood.

easy.question: What were the length and width of the altar?
easy.explanation: The passage states that the altar was five cubits long and five cubits wide.

easy.question: What covered the altar and its utensils?
easy.explanation: The altar and its utensils were made of or covered with brass.

medium.question: Why can we say that the burnt offering altar was square?
answers: Its length and width were equal
medium.explanation: Its length and width were both five cubits, so it was square.

medium.question: In the phrase “a brasen grate of network,” what was the grate?
medium.explanation: The phrase “of network” shows that the grate was mesh-like.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the staves inserted into the altar’s rings?
medium.explanation: The staves were placed in the rings so that the altar could be carried.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the altar was designed to be portable?
answers: The rings and staves used to carry it
The horns on its four corners
The fact that it was covered with brass
challenge.explanation: The rings and staves made it possible to carry the altar from place to place.

challenge.question: What did the altar and its staves have in common?
answers: Both were made only of silver
Both were made of shittim wood and covered with brass
Both were made only of brass
challenge.explanation: Both were made of shittim wood and covered with brass.

challenge.question: How far down did the brass grate extend?
answers: To the top of the altar
From the bottom up to the middle of the altar
challenge.explanation: The grate extended from the bottom of the altar up to its middle.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the altar was designed to be portable?
answers: The rings and staves used to carry it
The horns on its four corners
The fact that it was covered with brass
questions.explanation: The rings and staves made it possible to carry the altar from place to place.

questions.question: What did the altar and its staves have in common?
answers: Both were made only of silver
Both were made of shittim wood and covered with brass
Both were made only of brass
questions.explanation: Both were made of shittim wood and covered with brass.

questions.question: How far down did the brass grate extend?
answers: To the top of the altar
From the bottom up to the middle of the altar
questions.explanation: The grate extended from the bottom of the altar up to its middle.

easy.question: What were the laver and its foot made of?
easy.explanation: The verse says that both the laver and its foot were made of brass.

easy.question: What was used to make the laver and its foot?
easy.explanation: They were made from the looking-glasses of the women who assembled at the tabernacle entrance.

easy.question: Where were the women assembling?
answers: At the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
easy.explanation: The verse says they assembled at the door of the tabernacle.

medium.question: What can we understand from the fact that the laver was made from the women’s looking-glasses?
answers: Personal objects were used for the tabernacle service
The laver was used as a mirror
The women built the entire tabernacle
medium.explanation: The women donated personal objects, which were then used to make a vessel for the tabernacle.

medium.question: In the phrase “the women assembling,” what does “assembling” mean?
medium.explanation: The context indicates that the women gathered at the tabernacle entrance.

medium.question: Which detail is stated about both the laver and its foot?
medium.explanation: The verse says that both the laver and its foot were brass.

challenge.question: According to the verse, who owned the looking-glasses used to make the laver?
answers: The women who assembled at the tabernacle entrance
The priests who served in the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the looking-glasses with the women who assembled at the tabernacle entrance.

challenge.question: What was the difference between the laver and its foot?
answers: The laver was gold and the foot was brass
The laver was the vessel and the foot was its base
The laver was inside the tabernacle and the foot was outside
challenge.explanation: The foot was the base on which the laver stood.

challenge.question: What connection does the verse make between the mirrors and the women?
answers: The mirrors are described as new
The women are described as builders
The mirrors are linked to the women who gathered at the tabernacle entrance
challenge.explanation: The verse links the looking-glasses with the women who assembled there.

questions.question: According to the verse, who owned the looking-glasses used to make the laver?
answers: The women who assembled at the tabernacle entrance
The priests who served in the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The verse connects the looking-glasses with the women who assembled at the tabernacle entrance.

questions.question: What was the difference between the laver and its foot?
answers: The laver was gold and the foot was brass
The laver was the vessel and the foot was its base
The laver was inside the tabernacle and the foot was outside
questions.explanation: The foot was the base on which the laver stood.

questions.question: What connection does the verse make between the mirrors and the women?
answers: The mirrors are described as new
The women are described as builders
The mirrors are linked to the women who gathered at the tabernacle entrance
questions.explanation: The verse links the looking-glasses with the women who assembled there.

paragraphs.title: The Hangings of the Tabernacle Court

easy.question: What was the length of the court hangings on the south side?
easy.explanation: The passage says that the south-side hangings were one hundred cubits long.

easy.question: How many pillars were on the north side of the court?
easy.explanation: The north side had twenty pillars.

easy.question: What were the sockets of the court pillars made of?
easy.explanation: The sockets were made of brass.

medium.question: What was the similarity between the south and north sides of the court?
answers: Both had one hundred cubits, twenty pillars, and twenty sockets
Both had fifty cubits and ten pillars
Both had a gate in the center
medium.explanation: Both sides had the same length and the same number of pillars and sockets.

medium.question: What can we infer from the fifteen-cubit hangings on each side of the gate?
answers: The gate was on the north side
The gate lay between two equal sections
The gate was made of silver
medium.explanation: The gate was between two equal sections, each fifteen cubits long.

medium.question: In the phrase “the hooks of the pillars and their fillets,” what were the fillets?
answers: Rings or connections around and joining the pillars
medium.explanation: The context indicates that the fillets were fittings that connected or strengthened the pillars.

challenge.question: Based on the measurements of the east side, what was probably the width of the gate?
challenge.explanation: The east side was fifty cubits wide. After subtracting fifteen cubits on each side, twenty cubits remained for the gate.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the court was surrounded by hangings on every side?
answers: The mention of silver pillars alone
The statement that all the court hangings were round about
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly says that all the court hangings were round about.

challenge.question: What common ratio appears between the length of the hangings and the number of pillars?
challenge.explanation: On the different sides, the measurements consistently equal five cubits for each pillar.

questions.question: Based on the measurements of the east side, what was probably the width of the gate?
questions.explanation: The east side was fifty cubits wide. After subtracting fifteen cubits on each side, twenty cubits remained for the gate.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the court was surrounded by hangings on every side?
answers: The mention of silver pillars alone
The statement that all the court hangings were round about
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says that all the court hangings were round about.

questions.question: What common ratio appears between the length of the hangings and the number of pillars?
questions.explanation: On the different sides, the measurements consistently equal five cubits for each pillar.

paragraphs.title: The Court Gate and the Pins

easy.question: What is described in verse 18?
answers: The hanging of the court gate
easy.explanation: The verse describes the court gate hanging, including its measurements and materials.

easy.question: What was the length of the court gate hanging?
easy.explanation: The verse says that its length was twenty cubits.

easy.question: What were all the pins made of?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the pins of the tabernacle and court were brass.

medium.question: What can we understand from the comparison between the gate hanging and the court hangings?
answers: The dimensions of the gate hanging were compared with those of the court hangings
The gate hanging was made only from the court hangings
The hanging was placed outside the camp
medium.explanation: The verse gives the gate hanging’s dimensions in relation to the court hangings.

medium.question: In what order are the details in verses 18–20 presented?
answers: The pins, the hanging, the pillars
The hanging, the pillars, the pins
The pillars, the pins, the hanging
medium.explanation: The passage first describes the hanging, then its pillars and sockets, and finally the pins.

medium.question: In “answerable to the hangings of the court,” what does “answerable to” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase compares the gate hanging’s dimensions with those of the court hangings.

challenge.question: According to the measurements, what was the ratio of the hanging’s length to its other measurement of five cubits?
answers: The length was four times as great
The length was twice as great
The length was equal to it
challenge.explanation: The length was twenty cubits, which is four times five cubits.

challenge.question: What explicit numerical relationship is given for the pillars and sockets?
challenge.explanation: The passage says that there were four pillars and four sockets.

challenge.question: What does “of the tabernacle, and of the court round about” show about the pins?
answers: They were only inside the tabernacle
They belonged only to the gate
They were around both the tabernacle and the court
challenge.explanation: The pins were placed around both structures.

questions.question: According to the measurements, what was the ratio of the hanging’s length to its other measurement of five cubits?
answers: The length was four times as great
The length was twice as great
The length was equal to it
questions.explanation: The length was twenty cubits, which is four times five cubits.

questions.question: What explicit numerical relationship is given for the pillars and sockets?
questions.explanation: The passage says that there were four pillars and four sockets.

questions.question: What does “of the tabernacle, and of the court round about” show about the pins?
answers: They were only inside the tabernacle
They belonged only to the gate
They were around both the tabernacle and the court
questions.explanation: The pins were placed around both structures.

paragraphs.title: The Accounting of the Tabernacle Work

easy.question: Who was responsible for the work of the Levites?
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Levite service was under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.

easy.question: Which tribe was Bezaleel from?
easy.explanation: Bezaleel was from the tribe of Judah.

easy.question: Which tribe was Aholiab from?
easy.explanation: Aholiab was from the tribe of Dan.

medium.question: What can we understand from the fact that the Levite work was under Ithamar?
answers: The work had organized supervision and responsibility
The Levites did not work in the tabernacle
Ithamar built the entire tabernacle alone
medium.explanation: The wording shows that Ithamar was responsible for supervising the Levite work.

medium.question: What was the relationship between Bezaleel and Aholiab?
medium.explanation: The passage says that Aholiab was with Bezaleel, meaning he worked alongside him.

medium.question: In the phrase “an engraver, and a cunning workman,” what does “cunning workman” mean?
answers: A person who could not hear
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Aholiab as a skilled artisan, not as someone unable to hear.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Bezaleel being from Judah and Aholiab from Dan?
answers: People from different tribes participated in building the tabernacle
Only people from Judah worked on the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The tribal affiliations show that people from different parts of Israel worked together.

challenge.question: What does “with him” show about Aholiab’s role?
answers: He worked alongside Bezaleel and assisted him
challenge.explanation: “With him” means that Aholiab was a partner in the work.

challenge.question: Which description correctly combines the roles in the passage?
answers: Ithamar built all the tabernacle vessels, and Bezaleel supervised the Levites
Aholiab commanded Moses, and Bezaleel worked only with colors
Bezaleel did what was commanded, Aholiab worked with him as a craftsman, and Ithamar supervised the Levites
challenge.explanation: The passage presents these three distinct roles.

questions.question: What can we infer from Bezaleel being from Judah and Aholiab from Dan?
answers: People from different tribes participated in building the tabernacle
Only people from Judah worked on the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The tribal affiliations show that people from different parts of Israel worked together.

questions.question: What does “with him” show about Aholiab’s role?
answers: He worked alongside Bezaleel and assisted him
questions.explanation: “With him” means that Aholiab was a partner in the work.

questions.question: Which description correctly combines the roles in the passage?
answers: Ithamar built all the tabernacle vessels, and Bezaleel supervised the Levites
Aholiab commanded Moses, and Bezaleel worked only with colors
Bezaleel did what was commanded, Aholiab worked with him as a craftsman, and Ithamar supervised the Levites
questions.explanation: The passage presents these three distinct roles.

paragraphs.title: The Weight of Gold Used for the Holy Work

easy.question: What material is weighed in the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse records the gold used for the holy work.

easy.question: How many talents of gold were there altogether?
easy.explanation: The verse says there were twenty-nine talents.

easy.question: What work used the gold described here?
easy.explanation: The gold was used for the work of the holy place.

medium.question: What was the total amount of gold according to the verse?
answers: Twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels
medium.explanation: The verse gives both the number of talents and the additional shekels.

medium.question: In the phrase “the gold of the offering,” what does “offering” indicate?
answers: Gold lifted up or given as a contribution
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to gold donated for the holy work.

medium.question: Why does the verse mention both talents and shekels?
answers: To state the weight more precisely
medium.explanation: Talents give a large unit of weight, while shekels specify the remainder.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “All the gold that was occupied for the work”?
answers: The verse counts only the gold actually used for the holy work
The gold was stored and not used
The gold was used only for private jewelry
challenge.explanation: The phrase limits the count to gold used in the holy work.

challenge.question: What does “after the shekel of the sanctuary” mean?
answers: The gold was weighed only at the Temple
The weight was measured according to a sacred standard
The gold was shaped only as shekels
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the official standard of the sanctuary.

challenge.question: Which word emphasizes that the amount is a complete total?
challenge.explanation: The word “all” introduces the complete total.

questions.question: What can we infer from “All the gold that was occupied for the work”?
answers: The verse counts only the gold actually used for the holy work
The gold was stored and not used
The gold was used only for private jewelry
questions.explanation: The phrase limits the count to gold used in the holy work.

questions.question: What does “after the shekel of the sanctuary” mean?
answers: The gold was weighed only at the Temple
The weight was measured according to a sacred standard
The gold was shaped only as shekels
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the official standard of the sanctuary.

questions.question: Which word emphasizes that the amount is a complete total?
questions.explanation: The word “all” introduces the complete total.

paragraphs.title: The Census Silver and the Holy Sockets

easy.question: What was the total amount of the silver collected from those counted?
answers: One hundred talents of silver and 1,775 shekels
easy.explanation: The passage gives a total of one hundred talents plus 1,775 shekels.

easy.question: At what age were people included in the census?
easy.explanation: The census included everyone twenty years old and upward.

easy.question: What was done with the silver remaining after the sockets were made?
answers: It was cast into the holy vessels
It was used to buy animals
It was made into hooks for the pillars, and used to overlay and fillet them
easy.explanation: The remaining silver was used for the pillars’ hooks, capitals, and fillets.

medium.question: How much did each person counted contribute?
medium.explanation: Each person counted gave half a shekel.

medium.question: In “the sockets of the sanctuary,” what were sockets?
medium.explanation: Sockets were the bases or supports for the pillars.

medium.question: What was the order in which the silver was used?
answers: Hooks were made first, and then the silver was collected
The pillars were overlaid first, and then the people were counted
The sockets were cast first, and the remaining silver was used for the pillars
medium.explanation: One hundred talents were used for the sockets, and the remainder for the pillars.

challenge.question: What can we infer from one hundred talents being used for one hundred sockets?
answers: One talent of silver was used for each socket
Half a talent was used for each socket
Only fifty sockets were made of silver
challenge.explanation: The passage states that there was one talent for each socket.

challenge.question: Which calculation matches the silver collected in the census?
answers: 603,550 people gave half a shekel each
challenge.explanation: There were 603,550 people counted, and each gave half a shekel.

challenge.question: What does “for every one that went to be numbered” show about the collection?
answers: Only the wealthy had to pay
Each family paid according to its animals
Every person counted paid a fixed amount
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the same amount was required from each person counted.

questions.question: What can we infer from one hundred talents being used for one hundred sockets?
answers: One talent of silver was used for each socket
Half a talent was used for each socket
Only fifty sockets were made of silver
questions.explanation: The passage states that there was one talent for each socket.

questions.question: Which calculation matches the silver collected in the census?
answers: 603,550 people gave half a shekel each
questions.explanation: There were 603,550 people counted, and each gave half a shekel.

questions.question: What does “for every one that went to be numbered” show about the collection?
answers: Only the wealthy had to pay
Each family paid according to its animals
Every person counted paid a fixed amount
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the same amount was required from each person counted.

easy.explanation: The verse explicitly refers to brass.

easy.question: How many talents of brass were there?
easy.explanation: The verse says there were seventy talents.

easy.question: What was made from the brass?
answers: Only the Ark of the Covenant
The sockets of the tabernacle door, the brass altar, and its utensils
easy.explanation: The brass was used for sockets, the altar, the grate, and the altar’s utensils.

medium.question: What is the relationship between verses 29 and 30?

Verse 30 describes the collection of gold
Both verses deal only with priestly garments

answers: Brass lifted up or dedicated as a contribution

medium.question: What happened first according to the order of the verses?

The amount of brass was stated and then its use was described
The tabernacle was built and then the brass was collected

challenge.question: What can we infer from “all the vessels of the altar”?

easy.question: What was around the court?

easy.question: What are the pins mentioned in the verse associated with?

medium.question: What can we understand from the mention of the court-gate sockets?

The gate was made only of cloth
The gate was outside the tabernacle

medium.question: In the phrase “all the pins of the tabernacle,” what were pins?

They were equipment used for both structures

The mention of the pins alone
